An **agent trace** is a record of the observable steps an AI agent takes while handling a request. It often groups events such as model calls, tool calls, handoffs to other agents, and their results into one end-to-end workflow. Depending on the system and its settings, a trace may also include inputs, outputs, timestamps, status, and other metadata.

**Example:** A user asks, “What’s the weather in Boston?” The trace might show:
1. The agent receives the request.
2. The model decides to call a weather tool.
3. The tool returns the forecast.
4. The model produces the final answer.

A trace is different from the **final answer**, which is just what the agent returns to the user. It is also different from a **single log entry**: a trace typically links multiple events belonging to the same request. Traces describe observable activity; they do **not** necessarily include private reasoning. Exactly what they contain varies by framework and configuration.

**Sources:** [OpenAI Agents SDK tracing](https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/tracing/) describes traces as workflows composed of spans, including agent runs, model generations, tool calls, and handoffs. [LangSmith observability concepts](https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/observability-concepts) describes traces as the steps involved in an application execution.
